subject: starfish
subject_guess: Starfish (sea star), 5-armed, viewed with arms spread in the XY plane; radially symmetric, so "head" does not apply
readings: No head: radial (5-fold) body, disc fused with no protruding head/neck. The XY panel shows the full star outline (all 5 arms) and is used as the profile view for arm lengths/directions. The ZY panel shows one arm's edge-on curl plus the domed central disc (rings at z=8-16, y=8-16). The XZ panel shows the left/right arm pair edge-on plus the same domed disc (round blob z=8-16 at x=8-16).
disc center approx (12,12) in XY panel, taken as the body root

disc thickness: ZY/XZ panels show central bulge from z=8 to z=16 (and matching y=8-16), consistent with disc center z=12, thickness ~8 units, negligible compared to arm spans so arm z-direction taken as 0
notes: Starfish/sea star: radial body with no distinct head (disc is fused trunk, no protruding neck/lobe), so per the head-protrusion rule it contributes no leaf. Each of the 5 arms is a single unsegmented ray/limb (no internal joints visible in the mesh), so each arm is modeled as one segment from the disc center directly to its tip - lengths taken as straight-line (Euclidean) distance from the estimated disc center (12,12) to each arm tip as read in the XY panel, converting grid-y (down-positive) to frame-dy (up-positive) via dy = -(y_tip - y_center). Arm z-components are taken as 0 because the whole star lies essentially flat in the XY plane; the ZY/XZ panels only reveal the disc's small dome thickness (~8 units) and a slight out-of-plane curl at one arm's very tip, which is not encoded since we author proportional limb length/direction, not pose/curl. Two mirrored arm pairs (arm_L1/arm_R1 nearer the "front" and arm_L2/arm_R2 nearer the "back") were identified by their near-mirror positions about the vertical centerline in the XY panel; arm_C sits on that centerline and is unpaired, consistent with the 5-fold (pentaradial) body plan having one axis of bilateral symmetry through one arm.
